Variants.Content: Vaes Athjikhari is located on the Dothraki Sea inland from Essos, politically within the steppe world of Dothraki khalasars. It is a castle mainly responsible for local garrison, tax collection and sheltering the nearby population. Walls and roads tied the surrounding population, storage, and garrison here; even if the flags were changed, this stronghold would still affect how nearby people paid taxes, traded, and sought refuge.

Entry Vaes Athjikhari Local families also relied on pastures, horses, river branches, migration routes, and tribute from distant towns; if any road, well, spring, or wharf failed, the price would fall first on them.

Entry Vaes Athjikhari They also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of the Dothraki Sea; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, and true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hoof.

Entry Vaes Athjikhari If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

Ves Asgiha Kali is not just the main hall; the stone walls, wooden beams, iron doors, tombs and seams left by generations of repairs are also shaped here by the fears and legends left by the horse god, the starry sky and the khalasas. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Vaes Athjikhari They care about pastures, herds of horses, river branches, migration routes, and tributes from distant towns. They also look at whether seeds are left after harvesting grain, and whether city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
